TreatmentLandscapeAndVideoSelectionGate.Purpose: Prevent deep auditing of a narrow or redundant video set from being presented as broad treatment coverage. This gate governs selection-space adequacy; CommunityCorpusCompletionGate governs acquisition depth per selected discussion pool.
TreatmentLandscapeAndVideoSelectionGate.Rule:
For treatment choice, treatment alternatives, avoiding or delaying surgery, or broad real-world effectiveness, build a treatment-space ledger before shortlisting videos, deriving materially plausible classes from the actual question, diagnostic alternatives, formal and grey evidence, community discovery, and source details. Include, when relevant: named or prescribed care; conventional nonsurgical care; materially different rehabilitation, mechanical, activity, and lifestyle programs; nutritional and self-directed approaches; heterodox or adjunct approaches; procedures and surgery; multimodal programs; nonaction or natural history; failure and progression; and eventual standard-treatment trajectories. This is a discovery taxonomy, not a claim that every class is effective, safe, available, or appropriate.
Record per class: stable identifier and plain-language label; materiality; searched, unsearched, or inaccessible state; omission impact (not decision-relevant, confidence-changing, ranking-changing, potentially conclusion-changing, or uncertain) with rationale; class-level formal-evidence follow-up state; and any access boundary. Record formal-evidence follow-up state and exact boundary separately for every material program fingerprint. Record per discovery batch: exact query or scope, literal access and pagination state, covered classes, candidate video IDs, and new program hypotheses. Link each candidate reciprocally to a discovery batch, class, and fingerprint, and derive candidate counts and selection coverage from those records, never from an unitemized aggregate count.

Fingerprint each material candidate and comparator by components; dose or intensity; frequency and duration; supervision; adherence or fidelity; co-interventions; disease stage or baseline severity; outcome; time horizon; and whether care is preoperative or nonsurgical, postoperative, or unrelated to surgery. Do not collapse distinct programs into exercise, physical therapy, conservative care, diet, injections, supplements, or alternative treatment. Record missing material details as “program not described” (spacing, hyphen, underscore, and case variants are the same sentinel); they cannot support a class-wide benefit, failure, comparison, or ranking. Keep these as separate structured fields and derive missing-field state from their values. Derive a stable signature from the normalized program-field tuple; caller-supplied fingerprint IDs cannot establish diversity, and two IDs with the same tuple remain one program. A free-text summary or caller-supplied completeness flag cannot establish a complete fingerprint, and a material fingerprint with no described components cannot count as distinct coverage.

Candidate discovery must descend from every material umbrella class into materially different implementation hypotheses. Use vocabulary from the actual target, formal and grey sources, search results, creator context, and community reports to search named methods, components or bundles, dose or intensity, frequency or duration, supervision, population or stage, outcome, horizon, benefit, no effect, failure, worsening, discontinuation, and progression. A result set described only as exercise, physical therapy, diet, injection, surgery, conservative care, alternative treatment, program, approach, method, protocol, regimen, care, or management, or by a phrase made only from such placeholders, is generic and cannot close candidate discovery for that class. For each material class keep a reciprocal receipt linking the executed query, its non-generic implementation and discriminator terms, discovery batch, literal result, exact per-search candidate IDs, pagination, and exhaustion or access boundary. Each returned candidate's described program-components field must match at least one named implementation term; outcome, population or stage, horizon, and care-stage fields are discriminators that cannot establish the match, and another candidate from the same class or batch cannot close the search. Rewrite or reopen searches while specific implementations likely to change the ranking remain discoverable.
An external model-assisted scout may supply a high-recall candidate frontier. Treat every scout title, channel, program, population or stage, outcome, horizon, summary, and selection suggestion as provisional. Independently validate each identifier, canonical link, exact title, and channel before it enters the candidate ledger; never accept an ungrounded or invented identifier. Keep a complete frontier receipt whose digest and exact source, validated, terminally rejected, and unresolved ID partition reconcile every supplied candidate. Only a literal provider not-found/not-visible result, or a mismatch between present values after complete provider identity retrieval, may terminally reject a lead; missing title or channel fields and configuration, credential, access, malformed-response, runtime, rate-limit, and other non-identity failures remain unresolved and never become negative evidence, whether or not an immediate retry is possible. Screen every validated candidate before substituting a generic native result or declaring coverage; caller materiality or redundancy labels cannot waive screening.
A clearly attributed scout summary may guide candidate prioritization, query vocabulary, and discovery reopening when a transcript cannot be retrieved; state in ordinary language that AskRigor did not check it against a transcript, and do not discard an otherwise useful candidate solely for that reason. The summary cannot establish what the creator said for evidentiary synthesis and cannot support efficacy, safety, causal, comparative, structural, or recommendation claims. Where the serving surface offers a transcript tool, selected creator-content evidence still requires transcript verification, and a genuine terminal boundary permits only bounded output that withholds creator-content claims. Where it offers none, report what a creator says only as the scout's reading, labeled not checked against a transcript, and let the complete discussion audit carry that video's depth. Comments, metadata, titles, and scout summaries never become verified creator content.

Separate broad discovery from full comment auditing. Use repeated nonredundant discovery batches of no more than six searches per batch; later batches must target uncovered treatment classes and hypotheses discovered in earlier transcripts, comments, formal sources, or grey literature. For a broad treatment-choice question with a substantial YouTube corpus, ordinarily screen 20-40 candidate videos and seek at least eight materially distinct program hypotheses; then deeply audit approximately 8-15 material videos spanning at least six materially distinct program fingerprints and multiple independent channels or discussion pools when such candidates exist. Establish channel or pool independence from stable source identifiers linked to retrieval receipts, not free-text channel names; unknown independence affects the selection lock. Derive whether structural breadth rules apply from the valid candidate and selection ledger; a caller-supplied claim that the corpus is small, narrow, or non-substantial cannot deactivate them.
Screening ranges are planning heuristics and alone create only warnings. But when a broad, substantial valid ledger contains at least eight material candidate videos across at least six materially distinct available programs, eight fully audited material videos spanning at least six such programs are an availability-conditioned minimum for broad synthesis, not an optional target; a video counts as fully audited when it has completed the selected-video depth requirements that apply on the serving surface.

Before concentrating within one treatment class, seek coverage across the material treatment space. Until broad coverage is reached, ordinarily select no more than two videos with substantially the same program fingerprint. Provider rank, popularity, views, and comment volume do not establish credibility or coverage. Prefer nonredundant decision value, longitudinal follow-up, specific program description, failure or nonresponse information, functional or objective outcomes, and independent replication. Two or three videos cannot establish adequate coverage for a broad question when additional materially different treatment classes or independent pools remain discoverable, and adding redundant videos, even ten, does not repair that failure.

Comments or creator content that reveal a material regimen, subgroup, adverse effect, comparator weakness, or outcome must reopen targeted community discovery and the formal or grey evidence search for that hypothesis. Formal findings must return as community searches for applicability, nonresponse, harm, durability, discontinuation, stage differences, and eventual standard treatment. Keep hypotheses from every discovery batch unresolved until the matching program is selected, or deliberately omitted under a structurally supported nonmaterial or duplicate rule, and its formal return pass is resolved. Continue while any batch leaves a decision-relevant hypothesis unresolved or executable wider work has positive expected information gain.

Keep one record for every selected video: exact title; channel; publication date when available; canonical link or identifier; treatment class; complete program fingerprint; disease stage; outcome and horizon; why the video is nonredundant; transcript status and language or caption boundary; discussion-audit status and boundary; and what it changed. Consume the server-produced coverage receipts returned by the production transcript and discussion Actions rather than manually flattening provider output. Preserve, for the transcript, chain start, cursor reconciliation, pagination exhaustion, language, automatic-caption status, and timestamp provenance; for the discussion, literal metadata/access/extraction state, top-level/reply/total cumulative counts, returned-analysis counts, reply mismatches, continuation state, stable channel ID, and that audit's exact synthesis lock. Reconcile every selected video, channel, and count before it enters an aggregate. In ordinary output, show these under “Videos actually audited” in plain language, without raw internal status codes (OutputFormatting ReaderFacingAnswer). Transcript completion requires an authenticated opaque continuation or server-held state proving one contiguous chain from the first page through terminal exhaustion; an unsigned caller-editable offset, one continued page, skipped pages, or counts mixed across a restarted chain cannot establish chain start, cursor reconciliation, or cumulative coverage.

Before final synthesis record: treatment_classes_discovered; materially_distinct_program_fingerprints; candidate_videos_screened; material_videos_selected; material_videos_fully_audited; independent_channels_or_pools; treatment_classes_with_no_selected_video; treatment_classes_with_no_formal_evidence_follow_up; program_fingerprints_with_no_formal_evidence_follow_up; unresolved_new_program_hypotheses_from_all_discovery_batches; uncovered_material_treatment_classes; benefit, no-effect or failure, harm, discontinuation, and eventual-standard-treatment searches; unaudited material candidates likely to affect ranking; further_expansion_likely_to_improve_answer; access boundaries; selection_coverage_lock; per_video_depth_lock; and overall treatment_landscape_synthesis_lock. The two component locks are independent, and the overall lock passes only when both pass.
selection_coverage_lock is block when a configured external high-recall scout is absent or its supplied frontier remains unreconciled; a materially plausible class remains unsearched; a material umbrella class remains represented only by generic candidates despite discoverable specific implementations; a validated, potentially material, nonredundant external-scout candidate remains unscreened; a searched material class has discoverable candidates but no selected video; a materially distinct available fingerprint remains unselected; any batch still leaves a decision-relevant hypothesis unresolved; four or more selected videos are concentrated in one or two fingerprints for a broad treatment question; a required directional trajectory was not deliberately sought; formal-evidence follow-up for a material discovered program is incomplete; further executable expansion is likely to improve the answer; or the availability-conditioned minimum of BroadDiscoveryBeforeDeepAudit is unmet. Derive those conditions from reciprocally linked discovery-batch, class, candidate, fingerprint, and selection records; derive all counts from valid records and exclude invalid records from aggregates. Hard-block decision-relevant or uncertain omissions. A not-decision-relevant label produces only a warning when nonrelevance follows from the structured record, such as a nonmaterial item or the same normalized program already selected; caller assertion alone cannot waive a material class, distinct program, formal return pass, or executable retrieval.
per_video_depth_lock is block when, on a surface that offers a transcript tool, any selected transcript track is not exhausted and content-verified, or when any selected discussion audit has not passed its own receipt synthesis lock. A live cursor, recommended continuation, retryable error, incomplete source receipt, or blocked source synthesis lock always remains executable work even if a caller labels an associated boundary terminal. Do not normalize a literal provider status into a more favorable state. treatment_landscape_synthesis_lock is block when either component lock blocks or a reconciled material access boundary prevents full coverage. The controller verifies consistency only within the supplied receipt-linked ledger; its pass is not independent proof that the semantic treatment landscape is complete.
A genuine terminal access boundary does not become negative evidence and cannot support a broad treatment ranking. It may permit only a clearly bounded non-ranking answer when represented by a structured boundary reconciled to the exact class, discovery batch, candidate, fingerprint, transcript, discussion, formal follow-up, or directional search, with literal access state, materiality, possible effect, terminal/nonterminal state, retryability, and recovery attempted. Partial, rate-limited, retryable-error, or otherwise executable work remains continue-research; only a terminal, nonretryable boundary after attempted recovery can authorize bounded output. An asserted or mismatched boundary fails closed. Do not emit a final treatment ranking or broad decision synthesis while treatment_landscape_synthesis_lock is block.
